profile.headline: Software Engineer @ Amazon | UC Irvine CSE Alumna
profile.summary:
Hello!  I'm Citlali Rodriguez, a recent Computer Science and Engineering graduate from UCI.  Throughout my time as a student I have been exposed to both software and hardware fundamentals involving computers, and I have recently gained an interest in ML/AI.  As a result, I am currently seeking an internship or new grad position in software engineering, embedded systems, data science, or machine learning.  

I am a curious and dedicated student that is continuously seeking a new challenge.  These qualities enable me to quickly grasp concepts and adapt to unfamiliar environments.  When it comes to my work ethic, I take care to stay organized and take into account all details so that I may uphold a high standard of quality.  Additionally, I am an excellent communicator and have participated in multiple team projects where I have helped my group thrive.

In my professional life, I am ultimately looking for two key points.  The first is a position where I can continue learning and refining my skills.  The second is the opportunity to make an impact, whether by sharing my knowledge and helping my peers grow or through projects that leave a lasting, beneficial impact in our world. If these views resonate with you, feel free to reach out!

positions.title: Undergraduate Reader
positions.description:
- Upheld course reliability and efficiency by accurately grading over 600 student assignments within 24 hours

- Deepened student understanding by providing meaningful feedback on homework and exams

- Worked closely with fellow course staff to align grading standards, ensuring a cohesive and standardized evaluation process

company.name: UC Irvine Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences

positions.title: Learning Assistant
positions.description:
- Deepened student understanding by holding weekly office hours where students could receive 1-on-1 
   help

- Assisted during lectures by monitoring various, small groups of students working on assignments 
  and clarifying their questions using a metacognitive approach

- Maintained a smooth testing environment for a class of 300 students by proctoring, collecting and 
   sorting exams

-  Improved student experience by providing staff feedback on potential exams and by holding test 
   review sessions for students

-  Helped improve the course by collaborating with the professor and other learning assistants to assess 
   student progress and discuss potential changes to assignments

company.name: UC Irvine Donald Bren School of Information and Computer Sciences

honors.title: Dean's Choice Award
honors.description:
- Recognized as one of twelve outstanding teams, for the Biometric Advanced Driver-Assistance System, at UC Irvine’s Henry Samueli School of Engineering Annual Design Review

- Honored for highlighting and addressing the importance of driver safety, presenting a well-developed, mature project, and appealing to the curiosity of machine learning applications for both generalist and technical audiences
honors.issuer: Issued by Dean Magnus Egerstedt · Mar 2024

honors.title: Dean's Honor List
honors.description:
- 5 Quarters
- Award issued to students who are enrolled in at least 12 units and achieve a grade point average of 3.5 or 
  higher for that quarter

volunteerExperiences.description: Collaborated with an award-winning educator to facilitate hands-on physics and chemistry experiments, significantly boosting STEM engagement and comprehension among a diverse group of elementary school students, as evidenced by their increased enthusiasm for the subject matter

Supported fifth-grade teacher in preparing struggling students for the math section of the California Assessment of Student Performance and Progress exam by answering students’ questions, explaining difficult concepts in a clear manner by decomposing the problem, and engaging students with reflective questioning to foster understanding and self-assessment

projects.title: Biometric Advanced Driver-Assistance System
projects.description:
- Successfully established a Bluetooth connection between Zephyr BioHarness 3 and Windows computer systems, allowing for seamless live streaming of heart rate and breathing rate data between the driver and CARLA interface

- Successfully established an Open Sound Control connection between a Mindfield eSense Skin Response sensor and Windows computer systems, allowing for reliable live streaming of galvanic skin response between the driver and CARLA interface 

- Proficiently cleaned and analyzed 580,000 points of biometric data using Numpy, Pandas and Matplotlib libraries, extracting valuable insights from complex datasets

- Utilized Python’s Scikit-learn library in Jupyter Notebooks for machine learning algorithms, including Linear Regression, Naive Bayes, Decision Tree, Random Forest, and Neural Networks

- Rigorously implemented model evaluation methodologies, including cross validation, to ensure robustness and generalization of the model

- Continuously fine-tuned hyperparameters to achieve 82% model accuracy for stress classification

organizations.name: Video Game Development Club
organizations.description: I served as a gameplay programmer for a side-scrolling space themed game. Through this position, I learned to program using C# and Unity, and was able to sharpen my Git skills. I also routinely participated in weekly team meetings to discuss progress and future ideas, which gave me insight into project development with an interdisciplinary team.

organizations.name: Open Project Space
organizations.description: I joined UCI IEEE’s Open Project Space to advance my knowledge of embedded systems. Through this year-long membership, I gained hands-on experience in circuit design, soldering, breadboarding, microcontroller programming, hardware communication, and PCB design. I applied these skills in the creation of projects such as a miniature music player and RC car.
